commentaries.author: parimēlaḻagar
commentaries.text:
Her friend asks why she suffers so at evening, and she answers.

This sickness of desire is a flower. It buds in the morning, ripens all day into a full bud, and opens at evening. On waking she takes comfort in the union of her dream. As the day goes she forgets it and thinks of the parting. At evening she sees beasts and people drawn back to their mates, remembers her own joy, and can’t bear it.
